function: Radar-aided beam prediction: selects the best of 64 mmWave receive beams from FMCW radar range-angle maps, in a federated sensing-assisted ISAC link (pp. 3-4, Eqs. 6-7).
system: FMCW radar (3 Tx/4 Rx, 76-81 GHz) at base station; 60 GHz receiver with 16-element ULA, 64-beam codebook, omnidirectional transmitter; no RIS (p. 3 Fig. 1, p. 8 Table II).
method: Hybrid CNN-Transformer client models plus server linear layer, trained supervised (cross-entropy, Adam) with federated learning: clients upload features and gradients, server averages gradients (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: DeepSense 6G Scenario 9 development set, a real-world dataset: 5964 raw FMCW radar samples with 64-beam power vectors; used for both training and testing (p. 8).
test_conditions: 70/20/10% train/validation/test split of the same Scenario 9 data, partitioned randomly among 5 clients; also 2-5 clients and 1:9-9:1 train/test ratios (pp. 7-8, 11-12).
baselines: Learned only: FPN, LNRA (Demirhan and Alkhateeb), CNN-LSTM, ResNet, VGG, and own centralized No-FL variant; no non-learned baseline (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Top-k beam prediction accuracy for k=1 to 5; training and validation loss and accuracy curves (pp. 8-9, Eq. 26).
openness: Uses public DeepSense 6G Scenario 9 data (p. 8, ref. [47]); no code or data of its own released, no link given.
q1_support: p. 8: "we utilize the development dataset from Scenario 9 of the DeepSense 6G [47]"; p. 13, ref. [47]: "DeepSense 6G: A large-scale real-world multimodal sensing and communication dataset".
q2_support: p. 8: "we utilize the development dataset from Scenario 9 of the DeepSense 6G [47]" is the only data; p. 12: "experiments are conducted using various ratios of the training set to the testing set". No other scenario, site or band is tested; the 2-5 client sweep (p. 11) retrains per setting.
q3_support: p. 9: "The baseline models compared in this article and Ours (No-FL) all adopt a centralized training paradigm"; p. 10, Fig. 8: FPN, LNRA, LSTM, ResNet, VGGNet, all learned. No non-learned baseline (for example exhaustive beam search) is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "enabling rapid beam prediction in ISAC systems with limited computational resources" is only qualitative; Table I (p. 5) gives layer shapes only. No parameter count, FLOPs, complexity order or runtime appears in the paper.
q5_support: p. 8: "we utilize the development dataset from Scenario 9 of the DeepSense 6G [47]", a public dataset of radar signals and beam power vectors. The paper gives no link to its own code.
notes: Area 5 because the paper frames radar-assisted beam prediction as beamforming in an ISAC system (title, abstract p. 1; Fig. 1 p. 3); the alternative is area 3. Federated learning aggregates gradients digitally by arithmetic mean (p. 7), not over the air, so not area 7. The receiver has a 16-element ULA (p. 8, Table II), so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. The 'task offloading' in the abstract is the split of the model between clients and server, not a learned offloading decision. Tables I to III were read from the page images (pp. 5 and 8). Q1 rests on the DeepSense 6G real-world hardware data (Table II lists the radar and the 60 GHz receiver), although the word 'measured' is not used.
